source: Frey and Hirschi (2002) The effects of coupling on parameter design
finding: Human subjects adjusted sliders to hit output targets. Coupling made little difference at 2x2 but a huge difference from 3x3 to 5x5.
numbers: N=12 subjects. Target range 5% of gauge range. 2x2 coupled mean 40 s vs uncoupled 24 s (about 40% less), significant at alpha 0.05. 6x6 was dropped in pilots because many subjects quit.
limits: Tiny sample, abstract slider task with no domain knowledge, no pens or paper or tools. Many subjects quit at 6x6.
agent_relevance: Coupling hurts a bounded solver sharply once more than two goals interact. Our agent has a limited working context too, so keep coupled sub-goals few.
quote: coupling had only a moderate effect on the subjects' solution of the problem

source: Frey and Hirschi (2002) The effects of coupling on parameter design
finding: Time to solve uncoupled problems grew linearly with size. Time for fully coupled problems grew geometrically.
numbers: Uncoupled: linear fit adj R2 0.71 per-subject, 0.90 on means. Coupled: log-linear fit adj R2 0.70 per-subject, 0.99 on means; time proportional to 3.4^n, about 3x per added variable (n=2 to 5). Times normalised by each subject's own 2x2 coupled task.
limits: Fit built on four sizes only. Authors admit 2x2 differs qualitatively and the fit at n=2 may be coincidence. Distributions non-normal and skewed.
agent_relevance: Cost of tangled sub-problems explodes, so decomposing into near-independent parts is worth real effort (supports the decomposition operator).

source: Frey and Hirschi (2002) The effects of coupling on parameter design
finding: Subjects used different strategies by structure. Uncoupled: one slider at a time per output. Coupled larger: more iteration, more non-converging moves, random-sampling-like search.
numbers: Authors model coupled search as random sampling in a fixed-size n-dimensional target, giving geometric growth. Humans 3.4^n versus formal solve of order n^3 (2n^3+5n^2-7n operations); predictions differ by over a factor of two from n=2 to 5.
limits: Sampling model is offered as partial insight only. No bimodal split in completion times despite two strategies.
agent_relevance: An agent that tunes coupled knobs by trial and error will scale badly. Better to have it find the coupling structure first, then solve in order.

source: Frey and Hirschi (2002) The effects of coupling on parameter design
finding: Authors say the data support a weakened, human-centred reading of the Independence Axiom, not Suh's strong wording. Two coupled requirements can still be met.
numbers: Suh Theorem 9 says coupled designs cannot be manufactured; the data show 2x2 coupled tasks were solved with only modest extra time (about 16 s).
limits: Authors list cases where coupling helps: correlation among requirements can raise success probability, and coupled designs may be cheaper or simpler. Task far from real design.
agent_relevance: Do not make 'avoid all coupling' a hard guardrail. Treat it as a cost to trade off, strongest above two interacting goals.
quote: the need to avoid coupling is not self-evident and is not a general principle without counterexamples

source: Hirschi and Frey (2002) Cognition and complexity: an experiment on the effect of coupling in parameter design, Research in Engineering Design 13
finding: Journal version of the same slider experiment (title and DOI confirmed via Crossref; full text not opened).
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened, so no numbers taken from it. Check the journal for any larger sample than the ICAD paper.
agent_relevance: Follow-up to read if the series needs the journal numbers.

source: Goehler, Howard, Frey (2016) A model-based approach to associate complexity and robustness in engineering systems
finding: Model-based study of whether uncoupled designs are more robust. The independence axiom's robustness claim holds in general only for nominal-is-best requirements.
numbers: Abstract only: holds for nominal-is-best; fails for max-is-best and min-is-best; a machining example had a coupled design more robust than its uncoupled counterpart; for max/min requirements the contradiction level between coupled requirements has the strongest, statistically significant effect.
limits: Read the abstract page only; PDF download was blocked by a rate limit. Numerical simulation, not human or field data.
agent_relevance: Coupling is not the right quantity alone. Whether coupled goals pull against each other matters. A conflict check is more useful than a plain coupling check.

source: Goehler, Howard, Frey (2016) A model-based approach to associate complexity and robustness in engineering systems
finding: Practical rule from the same paper: if the main influences on each function are known early, contradiction level can rank concept robustness.
numbers: No further numbers read.
limits: Abstract-level only.
agent_relevance: Suggests a cheap early check the agent can run: list which goals oppose each other, not just which touch.

source: Mollajan, Iranmanesh, Khezri, Abazari (2022) Effect of applying independence axiom of Axiomatic Design theory on performance of an Integrated Manufacturing Information System, SIMULATION
finding: Simulation of a real manufacturing information system. Authors report that satisfying the independence axiom significantly improved performance.
numbers: Abstract only: Visual SLAM/AweSim simulation, logistic regression at each decomposition level, outcomes were time in process and utilised capacity. No effect sizes read.
limits: Single case, simulated not field-measured, author-reported abstract. Full text not opened.
agent_relevance: One of few quantitative supports for uncoupling; weak and single-system.

source: Alarm icon design study with axiomatic design (NYCU repository record, Taiwan)
finding: A Taiwanese study applied axiomatic design to alarm icons. A search snippet reports 96 chemical engineering undergraduates in six groups; results matched the method on identification correctness and judgment time.
numbers: N=96, six groups (from search snippet only). No statistics seen.
limits: Could not open the PDF (fetch returned a bare page). Authors and year unverified. Treat as unconfirmed.
agent_relevance: Weak lead only; do not cite numbers.

source: Search finding (2026): no controlled test of axiomatic design versus other design methods found
finding: An arXiv search for 'axiomatic design' returned 6 hits; none test the independence axiom with an LLM or compare AD against another method. Other searches (coupling, DSM, LLM) returned no results.
numbers: 6 hits for 'axiomatic design'. Only 2605.25735 mentions LLMs, and only in discussion. Crossref returns no LLM-axiomatic-design study either.
limits: Search coverage is limited. The WebSearch budget ran out and the OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv API calls were rate limited, so the 2020-2026 sweep is thin.
agent_relevance: Our agent can adopt the independence idea as an untested design heuristic, not an evidence-backed one.

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Single-author conceptual paper. Argues first-level (essential) functional requirements should be the same for any designer given the same needs, and that coupling at that level propagates irreversibly.
numbers: No experiments. Zero measured results.
limits: Opinion grounded in Suh's three books. Disputes Ang Liu's claim that framing varies by designer. Not peer-reviewed as far as seen (arXiv v1).
agent_relevance: Supports a guardrail: state the problem solution-neutrally and independently before choosing methods.
quote: problem formulation... is arguably the most critical step in every design framework

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Claims LLMs can help find design parameters and derived requirements but fall short at essential FRs because that needs abduction and abstract thinking.
numbers: No measurement. It cites ARC and other works for the claim that LLMs are weak at abduction; no AD-specific test.
limits: Unsupported by its own data; the ARC link is argument by analogy. Our own ARC results are a separate control.
agent_relevance: Treat as a hypothesis to test: have the agent propose requirement sets and check independence, then measure.
quote: LLMs perform well in induction and are increasingly capable of deductive reasoning, they still struggle with abduction

source: Homay (2026) A Deep Dive into Axiomatic Design, Part I: Problem Formulation
finding: Gives an example of how a bad requirement can be built: 'receive a call over electromagnetic waves' bakes a solution choice into the requirement and merges two ideas.
numbers: One worked example, no counts.
limits: Illustrative only. Author says LLMs can easily copy such bad formulation, with no test.
agent_relevance: A cheap test case for a requirement-hygiene check: does a stated goal contain a solution or two goals?

source: Homay (2025) Complexity and Coupling: A Functional Domain Approach
finding: Argues coupling lives in the functional domain, not in the code or hardware, so counting module links is the wrong measure.
numbers: Kitchen faucet survey: over 100 software engineers; more than 80% wrongly called the two-knob faucet an uncoupled design.
limits: Survey reported in one line, no method, wording or sampling given. Author is a proponent of Suh.
agent_relevance: If people misjudge coupling that often, an LLM judge of coupling needs checking against known answers.
quote: more than 80% of the participants incorrectly identified the left figure (4a) as an uncoupled design

source: Homay (2025) Complexity and Coupling: A Functional Domain Approach
finding: Review of software coupling definitions says they all describe physical links and miss the functional link between requirements.
numbers: No new data. Defines coupling by whether one design parameter affects more than one requirement.
limits: Position paper. Single author.
agent_relevance: Define coupling for the agent as goal-to-goal interference, not as shared text or shared steps.

source: Homay (2025) The Mythical Good Software
finding: Argues 'high cohesion, low coupling' is vague and that more cohesion is not always better; cites an Amazon Prime Video move from microservices back to a monolith.
numbers: Cited claim: 90% cost saving after the move (second-hand, from a reference in the paper).
limits: Anecdote, not a controlled study, and the saving is not checked here. Shows that splitting into more independent parts can cost more.
agent_relevance: Warns that fully decoupled decomposition has its own overhead; do not split without limit.

source: Homay (2025) How to Define Design in Industrial Control and Automation Software
finding: Reviews how software design is defined in industrial automation; says the field lacks a scientific design definition.
numbers: No quantitative result. Cites a thesis comparing event-based and scan-based execution.
limits: Position paper.
agent_relevance: Little for the agent beyond naming the problem.

source: Yoong, Palleti, Silva, Poskitt (2020) Towards Systematically Deriving Defence Mechanisms from Functional Requirements of Cyber-Physical Systems
finding: Used an axiomatic-design-inspired method on a water treatment plant testbed to derive invariants before build, then trained attack detectors on them.
numbers: Two invariants tested. Decision trees 100% accuracy on both; naive Bayes 100% and 93.75%. No false positives on the SWaT dataset or testbed. Two attack tests detected.
limits: Position paper, two invariants, no baseline against methods that skip the design analysis. Authors say results may not generalise. Not an LLM study.
agent_relevance: Shows decomposed requirement-to-parameter maps can feed checks, but no test of the independence axiom itself.

source: Qiang et al. (2026) A Systematic Comparison and Evaluation of Building Ontologies
finding: Uses 'axiomatic design' in the ontology-engineering sense (OQuaRE quality metrics such as coupling between objects), not Suh's theory.
numbers: Metrics scored on a 1-5 scale per ontology; not relevant to the independence axiom.
limits: Name clash. Do not count as evidence for Suh's axiom.
agent_relevance: Exclude from the evidence base; note the keyword trap.

source: Panarotto, Brahma, Isaksson (2023) Problem decomposition: the key to Agile sprints in Design Research, DSM 2023
finding: Applies the independence axiom with design structure matrices to split research problems so they can be run in parallel sprints. Shows a matrix for point-based versus set-based concurrent engineering.
numbers: Two illustrative examples, no sample or outcome statistics. Risk-of-change formula uses (1 - comprehensiveness) times (1 - timeliness).
limits: Illustration, not a test. Matrix entries are judged by the authors; the claimed benefit is untested.
agent_relevance: A usable pattern for splitting a research task into parallel sub-agents with few interfaces.

source: Wikipedia (2026) Axiomatic design
finding: Summary of the two axioms: maintain independence of functional requirements; minimise information content.
numbers: Page lists no experiments or criticisms.
limits: Secondary source. Notes a claim that AD fixes issues in Taguchi methods with no data.
agent_relevance: Confirms the base definitions; adds no evidence.

source: Frey and Hirschi (2002), reading of Suh's Theorem 9 and Theorem 15 wording
finding: The paper separates 'coupling is hard' (supported) from 'coupling makes design impossible' (not supported).
numbers: Same data as the first lines; 2x2 coupled tasks were all finishable.
limits: Only tests parameter design, not concept selection.
agent_relevance: Phrase any coupling guardrail as a cost, not a ban.

source: Absence of replication: no replication of Frey and Hirschi (2002) was found in this search
finding: Crossref and arXiv title searches turned up no direct replication or larger human-subject test of the coupling-scaling result.
numbers: 0 replications found in 3 Crossref queries and 4 arXiv queries.
limits: Searches were short and APIs were rate limited; a replication may exist in journals I could not reach.
agent_relevance: Treat the 3.4^n law as one small study.

source: The Use of the Independence Design Axiom As an Enhancement to QFD (1994)
finding: Early paper noting that QFD treats coupling as normal and even desirable, which conflicts with axiomatic design.
numbers: Abstract only (via Crossref), no numbers.
limits: Rival-view framing; no test.
agent_relevance: A competing stance: some methods embrace interaction between goals.

source: Competing view: Frey et al. versus Suh's strong reading (2002 and 2016 together)
finding: Two independent lines (human-effort experiment 2002; robustness model 2016) both soften the axiom rather than refute it.
numbers: Human: modest cost at 2x2, geometric cost at 3x3 to 5x5. Robustness: holds for nominal-is-best only.
limits: Both papers share an author (Frey); no outside check seen.
agent_relevance: The axiom is a conditional rule of thumb. Encode it with conditions.

source: Gap: no LLM or AI test of the independence axiom (2020-2026) found
finding: The only LLM-related axiomatic-design text found is a 2026 opinion section. No benchmark, no pass rates, no ablation of an independence check exists in what was reachable.
numbers: 0 measured LLM results across the sources opened.
limits: Search budget exhausted; a study may sit behind sources I could not reach.
agent_relevance: If we want evidence we must run it: compare agent plans with and without an independence check on coupled tasks.
